theory.intro: The bearing of $B$ from $A$ is measured **at $A$**: stand at $A$, face north, and turn clockwise until you face $B$. Because the bearing of $A$ from $B$ is measured at the other end of the same line, the two bearings are different.
facts: Draw a north line at the point named after the word **from** — that is where the compass rose sits.
North lines are parallel, so co-interior angles between a north line and the line joining the points add to $180^{\circ}$.
Angles at a point add to $360^{\circ}$, which turns an angle measured anticlockwise from north into a clockwise bearing.
Both bearings are written as three-figure true bearings, e.g. $064^{\circ}\text{T}$ and $244^{\circ}\text{T}$.
steps: Draw a north line at each point.
Mark the bearing that is given.
Transfer the angle using the parallel north lines.
Turn the angle into a clockwise bearing from north.

The marked angle is reflex because the turn from north at $A$ continues clockwise past south and west.
$280^{\circ}$

The word **from** names the point where the compass rose sits, so the bearing of $Q$ from $L$ is the marked angle at $L$.
The bearing of $Q$ from $L$ is $072^{\circ}\text{T}$.
The bearing of $L$ from $Q$ is measured at $Q$ instead, where the clockwise turn from north runs the other way along the same line, so it is a different angle.

$62^{\circ}-85^{\circ}+360^{\circ}$
